Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is trying to indicate that Iran is making concessions in this regard and that it is ready to open the Strait of Hormuz in just two days instead of seven, provided the Americans respond favourably to those seven points. He also talked about Iran’s readiness in terms of weapons – Iran has upgraded its armed forces capabilities. He said Iran has had favourable responses from its neighbours, referring to meetings that happened over the last week or so with Arab countries, and with Turkiye and Pakistan. He said the foreign ministers of those countries may visit Iran in the near future, adding that security should be the responsibility of the region’s countries. He’s basically explaining that Iran is in charge of Hormuz, Iran has communication with its neighbours, and Iran is ready – with its neighbours – to solve the problems of security and traffic through the Strait of Hormuz without the Americans or any other foreign powers. Akraminia added that Iran’s air force will emerge stronger and better equipped after the war. live-orange 24h ago ( 21:55 GMT ) Media analysis sheds light on Iranian attacks’ impact on US defence capacity in Middle East Iranian strikes on 26 US military bases in the Middle East targeted early-warning systems before hitting aircraft and buildings, causing billions of dollars in damage to equipment, an AP analysis has found, raising questions about US defences in the region and the potential for further strikes. The news agency found that, through August, more than 115 drone or missile strikes claimed by Iran or Tehran-backed armed groups and militias damaged or destroyed structures on 26 military bases and other sites with US equipment. The analysis showed that Iran initially focused its attacks on aircraft hangars and systems that detect incoming strikes, clearing the way for further attacks on warehouses, troop housing and more. The damage has significantly reshaped the US foothold in the Middle East, with two regional officials saying Washington has moved many of its assets out of the Gulf. Trump has said he is considering new strikes after Tuesday’s midterm elections. Tehran has promised to respond to any attacks in a manner yet unseen in this conflict. The AP independently verified damage to US targets using satellite imagery from multiple providers and spoke to four regional officials who were briefed or have firsthand knowledge of what was hit.
